title: November/December 2026
gist: Table of contents for Foreign Affairs' November/December 2026 issue, listing essays on US power limits, war technology, chokepoints, economic espionage, AI geopolitics and a possible AI bust, the US-Iran forever war, China's demographic decline and green path to ending dollar dominance, and reviews on liberalism and the global economy.

insights.claim: The issue's lead essays pair 'The Limits of American Power' (William McRaven) and 'The Fog of Tech' (Mara Karlin) with 'The Chokepoint Trap' by Henry Farrell, Abraham Newman and Yeling Tan, which the issue subtitles as how the search for economic security will end in geopolitical calamity.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Elite foreign-policy discourse is focused on limits of force and economic-security overreach.

insights.claim: The issue includes three AI essays with differing angles: 'Empires of AI' (Niall Ferguson, Lisa Klaassen, Eric Schmidt), 'The Global AI Bust' (Ruchir Sharma) on what survives when the boom ends, and 'AI Is a Choice' (Alex Imas, Mohamed El-Erian, James Manyika).
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: A prominent publication airing an explicit AI-bust argument is a sentiment datapoint for AI-trade positioning.

insights.claim: Two Iran essays appear, 'The New Forever War' by Ali Vaez (why America and Iran fight on without victory) and 'Why Iran Escalates' by Mohammad Ayatollahi Tabaar (Tehran's strategy to drive America out of the Middle East).
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Mainstream analysts frame the US-Iran conflict as a prolonged stalemate, not a near-term resolution.

insights.claim: The issue also covers China through Carl Minzner's 'China's Long Twilight' on demographic decline and political paralysis, and Zongyuan Zoe Liu's 'The China Price' on Beijing's green path to ending dollar dominance.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Highlights the narrative that China's renewables push is a vehicle for challenging the dollar.

insights.claim: Other pieces include David Cohen's 'The Case for Economic Espionage', exchanges on 'Who Killed the Global Economy?' with Nicholas Lardy and Michael Froman, and a debate on nuclear deterrence, 'Who Needs the Bomb?'.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Signals live policy debates on economic espionage and the roots of the next global economic crisis.
